title: Cross-team Acceptance Conductor — PRD checkpoint for multi-team clearance
creator: Diego Ramos
description: Goal: Drive a light-weight, auditable signoff process for the Private Deployment PRD (v2) so engineering, design, and legal reach consensus on scope, acceptance criteria, and rollout constraints. We need a clear acceptance conductor that sequences reviews, captures outstanding trade-offs (latency vs. isolation, quantization vs. fidelity), and provides a minimal set of gating artifacts for release approval. This ticket coordinates handoffs, documents open risks and compensating controls, and produces the final acceptance checklist for the release lead. Out-of-scope: detailed implementation tasks (stay in ENG tickets), full design spec iterations — we only require signoff-ready mocks and accessibility notes.
acceptance_criteria: PRD v2 final doc linked and versioned in Confluence
Design provides final mockset (desktop + mobile) and a compact rollout dashboard mock for Console
Engineering confirms performance delta with proposed KV cache change (measured in canary infra) and posts benchmark results
Legal signs off on data residency and customer contract clause for Private deployments
A canary rollout plan with success metrics and rollback criteria is documented and approved
Release lead has a one-page acceptance checklist and owner assignments for post-launch monitoring
comments: 2025-03-01 — Diego Ramos: Kickoff meeting notes posted. Stakeholders: Amira (PM), Priya Shah (Eng lead), Mateo Cruz (Design), Hana Kim (Legal). Action items: Priya to run KV cache microbenchmarks; Mateo to produce compact Console mock for rollout metrics; Hana to draft data residency clause. Linked artifacts above.

2025-03-03 — Priya Shah (ENG): Initial microbenchmarks show 6% mem increase with KV prefetch enabled but 18% token cost reduction on common prompt shapes. Proposal: enable KV prefetch behind a runtime flag and limit to dedicated pools for first canary. Blocking question for Legal on whether telemetry required for rollback is allowable under customer contracts.

2025-03-04 — Hana Kim (Legal): Drafted clause for Confluence: adds opt-in telemetry for rollback with defined retention (30d) and encryption at rest. Requests product confirm minimal telemetry fields. Suggested labeling for audit traceability in Console. Marking security_review_required true.

2025-03-05 — Mateo Cruz (Design): Uploaded compact dashboard mock (link). Dashboard focuses on per-route token-cost, canary region health, and rollback button with two-step confirmation. Accessibility notes included; wants engineering to confirm density of metrics is feasible in Console 2025.04 release.

2025-03-06 — Amira Patel (PM): Decision log: Accept Priya's proposal for runtime-flagged KV prefetch for canary only. Canary scope: two dedicated regions (us-west2, eu-central1) for 7 days, 10% traffic cap, automatic rollback if latency P95 increases > 12% or error rate > 0.5%. Follow-ups: Eng to post benchmark numbers for those region-sized pools; Design to annotate mock with failure state and rollback confirmation copy; Legal to provide final clause text for PRD. Assigned owners in comments and checklist.

2025-03-07 — Diego Ramos: Updated PRD with decision log and linked canary plan. Noted remaining trade-off: small chance of transient latency regression for short sequences under KV prefetch; documented mitigation: burst-capacity throttles and temporary fallback to non-prefetch path. Next step: 48-hour review window for final signoffs (legal/design/eng).
